text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A Gallup poll finds 27 percent of Lithuanians believe 1997 will be a better year, 36 percent see no change coming and 29 percent expect it to be worse.
- Food prices have increased already while energy tariffs have not gone up following the abolition of value added tax exemptions on food products and energy resources on January 1.

- Two groups of illegal immigrants, 43 and 11 people, were detained in Lithuania on the eve of the New Year. Nearly 2,000 have been detained in the country during 1996. Some 400 of them are housed in the Pabrade immigrant detention centre.
- Klaipeda sea cargo company Klasco re-loaded a record 7.6 million tons of cargo, 10 percent more than in 1995 and served 2,500 ships.

- Education and Science Minister Zigmas Zinkevicius does not intend to resign though his position towards national minorities caused a strong negative reaction of ethnic Poles in Lithuania and abroad.

- Lithuanian president Algirdas Brazauskas said the police and prosecutor's office failed to carry out their duties in investigating a case in Panevezys. Rimas Okulicius, a Pnevezys shop-keeper, shot four members of an organised criminal group and injured another four in self defence on the Christmas eve.
- Lithuanian Gas Company has decided to impose strict fines on consumers stealing gas.
- Lithuanian president Vytautas Landsbergis urged the Interior Affairs ministry and prosecutor's office to do everything to introduce "a strong-hand policy" in the legal system.

- The newspaper carries a list of 200 biggest enterprises in Lithuania based on the financial reports of nine months of 1996. The list is headed by Lietuvos Energija with turnover of 1.99 billion litas, Mazeikiu Nafta oil refinery with 684 million litas and Lithuanian Gas with 506 million litas.
- Two market-moving pieces of news are expected in mid-January. The Finance ministry is to decide on the state borrowing plan for 1997 and an IBCA credit rating for Lithuania will be made public.
- Statistics department forecasts for 1997 show 12 percent inflation and an increase in GDP of 4.5 percent.
